== Missing data ==
* No interview or article was found in which a ''My Little Pony'' CCG designer names SWCCG or Decipher as an influence.
* Lead designer Darrell Hardy's published bio lists Fantasy Flight Games and Sony Online Entertainment, not Decipher.
* Destiny draws in ''Young Jedi'' and ''Jedi Knights'': Wikipedia says both kept SWCCG's destiny draw, but the rulebooks were not checked, so the article does not say it.
* No source ties ''Star Wars: Destiny'', ''Star Wars: Unlimited'', ''Star Trek CCG'' Second Edition, ''Lightseekers'' or ''Netrunner'' to SWCCG.

== Possibly faulty data ==
* Ryan Jellison said the pair cards are "destiny five". ''Premiere'' (2013) pair Events have power 4; power-5 versions start with ''Canterlot Nights'' (2014). The article shows both.
* Other names in the ''My Little Pony'' rulebook credits match Decipher-era people (Dan Burns, Jason Winter, Michael Girard, Cheryl Kallenbach, Brigid Lischke). Same name only; not used.

== Build notes ==
* Jellison quotes checked against the audio of Bill Bisco's interview, 36:15–39:20.
* Card images from the PonyHead database; rulebook pages rendered from the Heart of the Cards copy of Enterplay's 2013 rulebook.

== 2026-10-15 uniqueness rewrite ==
=== Marginal cuts ===
* Entire "Not built on SWCCG" section: Wizards of the Coast ''Star Wars Trading Card Game'' (Garfield, "all new game mechanics"; Holland "totally incompatible") and Tom Lischke's LOTR quote "we have gone out of our way to do a lot of things differently" (Iain Lowson, [https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2002/02/14/26785-decipher-talks-lotr/ Decipher Talks LOTR], TheOneRing.net, 14 February 2002; Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261015183623/https://www.theonering.net/torwp/2002/02/14/26785-decipher-talks-lotr/ Internet Archive]). ''Star Wars Trading Card Game'' stays on its own page. LOTR is treated as influenced (uniqueness dots).
* ''My Little Pony'' CCG 2013 rulebook card-anatomy and faceoffs scans removed from the gallery. Cards plus the faceoff explanation remain. Rulebook still cited for the mechanic.

=== Build notes ===
* Wiki term is uniqueness dots (•), from [[Uniqueness]]. Diamond (◊) is a later deployment restriction.
* LOTR Comprehensive Rules 4.2: unique cards have a dot (•) before the title; non-unique cards do not. Unique page on wiki.lotrtcgpc.net: "Unique cards are indicated by a dot (•) to the left of the card title."
* Examples: ''Aragorn, Ranger of the North'' (1R89) Unique=Yes; ''Goblin Runner'' (1U178) Unique=No. Premiere [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] Unique; [[Stormtrooper]] Unrestricted.
* Young Jedi picture: ''Darth Maul, Sith Apprentice'' from Decipher's Menace of Darth Maul dark card list (Wayback).
